title: Shoot the planes (Eliminate Maximum Number of Monsters)
label: ag-multi
statement: Plane `i` is `dist[i]` metres above the ground and descends at `speed[i]` metres per second. Your gun fires once per second, starting at second 0. If any plane reaches the ground at or before the moment you would fire at it, the game ends. Return the **maximum number of planes you can shoot** before the game ends.
provenance: Reported in Agoda live-coding and OA rounds as "planes approaching the ground, one shot per second" — a variant of LeetCode 1921 (monsters → planes). Reported on LeetCode Discuss (DSA round), in an SSE Gurugram round (Oct 2025), a Jan 2026 Staff report and a Jan 2026 phone screen (FastPrep); CodeJeet scores 1921 at 98.6% for Agoda. Statement below is in my words.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Plane `i` is `dist[i]` metres above the ground and descends at `speed[i]` metres per second. Your gun fires once per second, starting at second 0. If any plane reaches the ground at or before the moment you would fire at it, the game ends. Return the **maximum number of planes you can shoot** before the game ends.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Does a plane that lands at exactly the moment I fire count as landed? (Yes — the game ends.)
- Are speeds always positive? (Yes; reject otherwise.)
- Could the arrays differ in length? (Reject.)
- How large is n — is O(n log n) fine, or do you want O(n)?

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Only the landing second matters, and only its ceiling: at integer second t you beat plane i exactly when t < ceil(dist/speed). Shoot planes in landing order; the i-th one is fired on at second i, so the first i with arrival <= i ends the game.

learn.title: 10 · Tests
learn.md:
**S1 — One gun**

- [1,3,4] at speed 1: all three
- [1,1,2,3] at speed 1: only one
- [3,2,4] / [5,3,2]: one
- lands exactly when you would fire = game over
- ceil, not floor: 5/2 lands at 2.5
- empty
- null
- lengths differ

**S2 — A faster gun**

- 2 per second clears [1,1,2,3]
- 2 per second: four planes landing at 1
- k = 1 matches the original
- k = 0 rejected

**S3 — A million planes**

- all far away: all shot
- in … ms (< 2000)
- int.MaxValue distance does not overflow

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Comparing dist/speed with integer division (floor) instead of the ceiling.
- Simulating second by second with a heap — correct but O(n log n) with more code than needed.
- Floating-point arrival times compared with ==.
- Off by one on "lands at the moment I fire".
